name: יְכָלְיָהוּ
gloss: Yahweh has prevailed; or Yahweh is able
summary: Jecoliah of Jerusalem, wife of Amaziah and mother of Azariah (Uzziah), king of Judah, who began to reign at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years (2Ki 15:2; 2Ch 26:3, spelled יְכָלְיָה). The name is the verb יָכֹל with יָהוּ: “Yahweh has been able” or “has prevailed”, the sense of Gen 32:29 and Jer 20:7. Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The name of his mother was יְכָלְיָהוּ of Jerusalem.”
“I know that you can do all things (כֹל תּוּכָל)”: the verb of the name, said of God.
“You were stronger than I, וַתּוּכָל”: Yahweh prevailing.

note: Takes j.bm.ac (1 token at 2Ki 15:2). The 2Ch 26:3 spelling יְכָלְיָה is not under a key of its own in BDB; check whether its token is counted. “Has prevailed” reads יְכָל as the perfect of the verb; the vowel pattern is not that of the usual perfect יָכֹל, so the reading is from the root, not the form.
